before the CDA & the Town Board of  the Town of Riverhead at their respective October 20, 
2026, meetings and further participate in the open comment period on any matter at the 
conclusion of the Agenda.  
PLEASE TAKE FURTHER NOTICE, that upon entering the Zoom meeting, you will be 
placed in a virtual audience. From there, you may either passively watch the public hearing 
live, or communicate to the moderator/host your request to make a comment during the 
public comment section for PUBLIC HEARINGS, RESOLUTIONS and/or OPEN 
COMMENTS. To alert the moderator/host of your desire to be heard, use the “CHAT” or 
“RAISE HAND” feature, then use the “CHAT” feature to inform the moderator/host of the 
following:

to speak.

and visible for the three-minute comment period. After three minutes, you will be placed back 
in the audience.

Councilman Kern offered the following resolution,

           WHEREAS, The Town of Riverhead regularly coordinates road restoration with National 
Grid after National Grid executes critical repair and maintenance to their utility lines throughout 
the Town. The Town of Riverhead Highway Department has received check #7003082807 from 
National Grid, in the amount of $329,459.28 representing a portion of the work associated with 
the 2026 Riverhead Gas Main Replacement Project, MSLI200099; and  
 
WHEREAS, due to recent weather, the road restoration project affecting Elton Street, 
Fishel Avenue, Howell Avenue, Howell Court, N. Howell Avenue, N. Howell Court, Brook Street 
and Prospect Place, may be delayed into the following fiscal year; and  
 
WHEREAS, prior payment made by National Grid for work on Edwards Avenue 
exceeded the expenditures of the project. The Highway Department has requested that the 
excess funds of $137,728.74 be transferred to the capital project account to absorb the costs of 
future National Grid roadway restoration projects. Now, therefore be it

budget adjustments;

SCULPTURE FOR DOWNTOWN RIVERHEAD 
 
Councilwoman Waski offered the following resolution,  
which was seconded by Councilman Rothwell 
 
          WHEREAS, Sherry Davis of Davis Fiber Arts, LLC, residing at 32 Crows Nest Drive, 
Riverhead, NY, donated a sculpture, titled “Grateful Turnout: A Public Thank You to First 
Responders”, with an estimated value of $20,000.00, to be installed downtown; and 
 
WHEREAS, pursuant to Town Law, § 64(8), the Town Board is expressly authorized to 
accept a gift “. . . for any public use, upon such terms or conditions as may be prescribed by the 
grantor or donor and accepted by said town, and provide for the proper administration of the 
same”; and 
WHEREAS, the Town Board finds that acceptance of this gifts, at no cost to the Town, is 
in the best interest of the residents of the Town of Riverhead as a meaningful, artistic display 
and representation of the community’s appreciation for first responders. Now, therefore, be it

sculpture, which utilizes decommissioned firehose and turn-out gear to honor all first 
responders, from Sherry Davis and Davis Fiber Arts, LLC; and be it further, 
RESOLVED that a copy of this resolution shall be forwarded to the Finance 
(finance@townofriverheadny.gov) and Community Development Departments; and be it further, 
RESOLVED, that all Town Hall Departments may review and obtain a copy of this 
resolution from the electronic storage device and, if needed, a certified copy of same may be 
obtained from the Office of the Town Clerk.

TOWN OF RIVERHEAD 
 
TB Resolution 2026-952 
 
AMENDS ORDER ESTABLISHING EXTENSION (NO. 97) OF BOUNDARIES AND FACILITIES OF THE 
RIVERHEAD WATER DISTRICT FOR FORGE ROAD, CALVERTON, NEW YORK, AT THE PROPERTIES 
KNOWN AS SCTM DISTRICT 0600, SECTION 118, BLOCK 5, LOTS 1.1, 1.2, 2 THROUGH 11 AND 12.1; 
SECTION 119 BLOCK 2, LOTS 59 THROUGH 62; AND SECTION 139, BLOCK 01, LOTS 1 THROUGH 4 
 
Councilwoman Merrifield offered the following resolution,  
which was seconded by Councilwoman Waski 
 
          WHEREAS, the Town of Riverhead (Town/Applicant for grant funding under the 2022 
Bipartisan Infrastructure Law) has identified the need to extend the boundaries of the service 
area of the Riverhead Water District (District) along with its existing distribution facilities to serve 
approximately seventy (70) mobile homes and fourteen (14) single family residences currently 
receiving potable drinking water from private wells; and 
 
          WHEREAS, limited water quality data for the private wells, indicates detections of 
contaminants or a likely potential for contamination in the form of poly and per-fluoroalkyl 
substances (PFAS), arsenic, iron, and manganese and further, while these wells are located 
adjacent to or within close proximity of the Peconic River and Peconic Lake, however the source 
of the non-naturally occurring contaminants is unknown; and 
   
          WHEREAS, the extension of clean water facilities is desirous now as wells are beginning 
to be impacted and the contamination level has been detected as approaching New York State 
drinking water standards; and 
 
           WHEREAS, the Riverhead Water District seeks to provide clean potable water through 
the installation of approximately 2,800 linear feet of water main at a projected revised cost of 
$1,520,000.00 exclusive of the costs related to installation of private service lines and key 
monies to be borne by property owners and 
    
          WHEREAS, the boundary of said proposed extension is set forth fully in the attached 
Exhibit A; and 
           
          WHEREAS, a revised map and plan dated November 2024 has been prepared by H2M, 
consulting engineers to the Riverhead Water District, detailing the necessary measures and 
costs associated with extending the Riverhead Water District facilities to service the subdivision 
and the development site and proposed residences; and 
           
          WHEREAS, the map and plan are available for review and inspection at the Office of the 
Riverhead Town Clerk, 4 West Second Street, Riverhead, New York, during normal business 
hours; and 
           
          WHEREAS, said map and plan calls for an extension of the existing water facilities and 
boundaries to provide service to approximately seventy (70) mobile homes, and fourteen (14) 
single family residences and the proposed extension is situated such that the District’s low 
pressure zone facilities can be extended from an existing 12-inch cement-lined ductile iron pipe 
Page 75 of 746
just north of NYS Route 25 on the southern end of Kroemer Avenue and total of approximately 
2,800 linear feet of new 8-inch water main will be required to serve the extension area with each 
residential dwelling will receiving a 1” water service and the mobile home parks receiving either 
4” or 2” water service based upon their respective sizes and finally, for firefighting purposes, five 
new fire hydrant assemblies will be required to provide the proper fire protection (a proposed 
layout of the proposed water mains and appurtenances and hydrants is contained was an 
exhibit to the map and plan); and 
           
          WHEREAS, the estimated project cost to implement Extension No. 97 has been 
estimated at $1,520,000.00 which costs include engineering, permitting, construction 
observation, legal, administration, contingencies, but excluding costs related to installation of 
private service lines and key monies to be borne by property owners; and 
           
          WHEREAS, on March 15, 2023, the Town was informed the project received grant 
funding under the 2022 Bipartisan Infrastructure Law – Emerging Contaminants in the amount of 
$1,185,000.00 and the balance of funds required to fund the project shall be from the Town 
Community Preservation Fund; and 
           
          WHEREAS, by Resolution #814 adopted on September 17, 2024, the Town Board 
amended Chapter 221 to create advisory board known as the Community Preservation Fund 
Water Quality Improvement & Pollution Prevention Committee with the duty and responsibility to 
make recommendations to the Town Board for identification of and/or set criteria for water 
quality improvement activities or pollution prevention projects to be included in the Town’s 
Community Preservation Fund Project Plan and by Resolution #877 adopted on October 16, 
2024, the Town did adopt an amendment to the Community Preservation Fund Project Plan 
setting forth criteria for water quality improvement activities or pollution prevention projects; and 
           
          WHEREAS, the Community Preservation Fund Water Quality Improvement & Pollution 
Prevention Committee have reviewed this project, Extension 97, and determined that such 
project meets the criteria and recommends that the Town Board authorize expenditure from 
Community Preservation Fund in the amount of $335,000.000 (total cost $1,520,000.00 less 
grant $1,185,000.00) necessary to fund the project with each resident responsible for the 
installation of their private service line from the meter pit to the residence including cost of the 
water meter, backflow prevention where appropriate, connection to internal plumbing, 
disconnect of existing private well from in-house plumbing or community water piping and well 
abandonment; and 
           
          WHEREAS, the single family homes currently on private wells that have the potential to 
be or have already been impacted by contamination are exempt from Key Money Fees and the 
existing commercial mobile home parks are subject to Key Money Fees of $2,047 per mobile 
home unit, and as such, the estimated seventy mobile homes spread across three properties 
the total Key Money Assessment is $143,290; and 
           
          WHEREAS, the proposed extension of water mains will be solely located within the public 
right-of-way of the Town of Riverhead and involves the extension of public water utilities to aid in 
the upgrade or replacement of private drinking water wells due to their impact or high 
susceptibility to being impacted by contamination; and, 
           
          WHEREAS, the Town Board held a public hearing on the 4th day of February, 2025 
regarding this proposed extension, wherein all persons wishing to be heard were heard, whether 
in person or in writing. 
Page 76 of 746
           
          NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS HEREBY ORDERED, that the Town Board of the Town of 
Riverhead as governing body of the Riverhead Water District hereby approves the extension of 
the existing water facilities and boundaries to accommodate water connection to provide water 
service to the properties to be benefitted by the proposed Extension No. 97 – Forge Road and 
designated as District 600, Section 118, Block 5, Lots 1.1, 1.2, 2 through 11 & 12.1, Section 
119, Block 2, Lots 59 through 62, and Section 139 Block 1, Lots 1 through 4 on the Suffolk 
County Tax Map, Riverhead, New York subject to the following conditions: 
1. The single family homes currently on private wells that have the potential to be or 
have already been impacted by contamination are exempt from Key Money Fees; 
2. The existing commercial mobile home parks are subject to Key Money Fees of $2,047 
per mobile home unit, the total Key Money Assessment spread across three 
properties containing approximately seventy mobile homes is $143,290; 
3. The Town Board shall authorize the application of the proceeds of grant funding under 
the 2022 Bipartisan Infrastructure Law – Emerging Contaminants for the full project 
cost or $1,185,000.00; 
4. The Town Board shall authorize expenditure from Community Preservation Fund in 
the balance amount of $335,000.000 (total cost $1,520,000.00 less grant 
$1,185,000.00) necessary for fund project; and, 
5. Each resident will be responsible for the installation of their private service line from 
the meter pit to the residence including cost of the water meter, backflow prevention 
where appropriate, connection to internal plumbing, disconnect of existing private well 
from in-house plumbing or community water piping and well abandonment. 
6. This Order shall take effect upon the acceptance and agreement by the applicant as 
set forth herein; and 
 
          BE IT FURTHER, RESOLVED, that the terms and conditions of this Order shall be 
accepted and agreed to by the Town, as applicant and recipient for grant funding under the 
2022 Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, whose consent shall be duly acknowledged and shall be 
binding on the heirs and assigns and shall run with the land and shall be effective upon filing 
with the Town Clerk; and 
          BE IT FURTHER, RESOLVED, that based on the guidelines provided by the New York 
State Department of Environmental Conservation (NYSDEC) in 6 NYCRR Part 617.5, the 
project can be considered a Type II project, requiring no further review; and 
           
          BE IT FURTHER, RESOLVED, that all Town Hall Departments may review and obtain a 
copy of this resolution from the electronic storage device and if needed, a certified copy of same 
may be obtained from the Office of the Town Clerk.

THIS TEMPORARY USE LICENSE AGREEMENT (“Agreement”) is entered into by  and 
between the Town of Riverhead Community Development Agency, an urban renewal agency  
under the Laws of the State of New York, whose address is 4 West Second Street, Riverhead, 
New  York 11901 (“CDA”), on the one hand, and BOLD Broadcasting LLC d/b/a BOLD Media, 
a  domestic limited liability corporation, with offices at 801 Motor Parkway Suite 102 
Hauppauge,  New York 11788 (“Licensee”), on the other hand. The CDA and Licensee shall 
individually be  referred to as a “Party” and jointly referred to as the “Parties”.  
WITNESSETH  
WHEREAS, as well known, recited and published, the property, former Calverton Naval  
Weapons Industrial Reserve Plant (hereinafter “EPCAL”), was formerly owned by the Navy and  
leased by the Grumman Corporation, and due to the decline in defense spending, in 1998, 
Northrop  Grumman closed nearly all facilities located on Long Island and chose not to renew its 
lease for  the EPCAL site; and  
WHEREAS, in 1998, the Navy conveyed 2900 (+/-) acres to the Town of Riverhead  
Community Development Agency for no consideration conditioned upon the Town’s reuse of the  
property for economic development; and  
WHEREAS, as part of this transfer, the CDA controls, owns, and maintains two (2)  
runways at ECPAL with the power to grant rights and privileges with respect thereto; and  
WHEREAS, BOLD Broadcasting LLC d/b/a BOLD Media desires to use approximately 
16 acres of the Western runway, tie down and taxiway at EPCAL designated as Runway 5/23 
(“Premises”) to conduct a drive-thru Christmas light show, in the area as shown and depicted on  
Exhibit “A” attached hereto and incorporated here by reference; and   
WHEREAS, BOLD Broadcasting LLC d/b/a BOLD Media has requested that the  
Community Development Agency grant BOLD Broadcasting LLC d/b/a BOLD Media a license  
agreement for this purpose; and  
WHEREAS, the Community Development Agency requests that the Town Board, as  
governing body of the Community Development Agency, authorize a revocable, non-assignable  
and non-exclusive license to BOLD Broadcasting LLC d/b/a BOLD Media to utilize the Western 
runway designated as Runway 5/23 which is part of the site known as EPCAL for the limited  
purpose of conducting a drive-thru Christmas light show; and  
WHEREAS, the parties have reached terms and conditions for such use.  
NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants, terms, conditions,  
privileges, obligations and agreements herein contained, and other good and valuable  
consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which is hereby acknowledged, the Parties mutually  
undertake, promise and agree, each for itself and its successors and assigns, as follows: 
 
Page 1 of 11 
Page 82 of 746
 
AGREEMENT  
A. Definitions/Recitals. The definitions and recitals set forth above are incorporated here by  
reference and made a part of this Agreement.  
B. Use of Premises. Licensee shall have the limited right to use a portion of the Western runway  
designated as Runway 5/23 at EPCAL and Licensors grant such rights and privileges as it may  
have to those facilities known as the runway, tie down and taxiways areas appurtenant thereto  
during the Term of this Agreement (defined below) for the limited purpose of conducting a drive  
thru Christmas light show. Public operation of the drive-thru Christmas light show shall occur 
between 5:00 pm and 11:00 pm. Licensee shall have reasonable access to the Premises at all times 
during the Term for installation, maintenance, deliveries, inspections, operation, repair, and 
removal of the light show and related equipment. No right to use of, or right to traverse  upon, 
any portion of grassland areas is granted. No cars, trucks, or other vehicles shall be parked 
overnight on the Premises except vehicles and equipment reasonably necessary for installation, 
maintenance, operation, security, or removal of the light show. Without limiting the foregoing, 
Licensee is expressly permitted to place and continuously maintain one semi-trailer on the 
Premises from delivery during installation through completion of final breakdown and removal. 
The semi-trailer may be used to store maintenance tools, replacement parts, supplies, and other 
equipment used in connection with the light show, and its presence shall not be deemed 
prohibited overnight parking, a permanent structure, or an unauthorized use of the Premises. The 
semi-trailer shall be positioned so as not to materially interfere with other authorized uses of the 
Premises and shall not be moved or removed by the Town or CDA during the Term except in an 
emergency or after reasonable prior notice and coordination with Licensee. The parties will work 
together in good faith to determine the positioning of the semi trailer and/or any other vehicles 
required to remain throughout the duration of the event such as to ensure convenient access for 
the show operators and to avoid conflict with other users of the property.  Any cones, barricades, 
or road equipment shall be temporary in nature and stored on the runway, or only those portions 
of the taxi area to which the  Town retains ownership, and out of the way of any traversing 
vehicles, and never on the grassland. Other than temporary light displays, signs, temporary 
ticketing/check-in booths, traffic-control items, temporary anchoring expressly permitted under 
Section J.3, and other items reasonably necessary for the operation of the light show, the runway 
shall be utilized as is, without permanent changes or alterations by Licensee. Temporary 
ticketing/check-in booths may be placed and maintained on the Premises throughout the Term in 
locations reasonably selected by Licensee, provided they do not materially interfere with other 
authorized uses of the Premises. Licensee may not use the Premises for any other purpose without 
the prior written approval by the CDA. In no event may Licensee use or permit the Premises to be 
used for any activity prohibited by federal, state, or local law.  
C. Term. The term of this Agreement shall be from October 26, 2026 to January 22, 2027,

 WHEREAS, the Town of Riverhead and the Riverhead Central School District wish

 NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants set forth herein,

 1.   The term of this Agreement shall commence upon the date of execution of 
this Agreement by both parties and terminate three (3) years therefrom unless earlier 
terminated as provided for therein.   
 
 2. The Town of Riverhead and the Riverhead Central School District each

Constitution and Article 5-G of the General Municipal Law to enter into intergovernmental 
agreements.

it to be in the best interest of their taxpayers, do hereby authorize inter-municipal 
agreement for the Town of Riverhead to provide salt and/or salt and sand mixture to the 
Riverhead Central School District.

$75.00 per payload bucket (3 yards) of salt and/or salt/sand mixture, subject to  Highway 
Department determination of adequate supply amounts necessary and appropriate by the 
Highway Department to perform its salt/sanding operation on Town roadways. Except as 
set forth in the preceding sentence, there is no maximum number of times in a daily period 
that this service can be provided.

status during the period of this agreement. The Riverhead Central School District shall

contemplated under this Agreement.  All policies shall provide for at least thirty (30) days 
written notice of cancellation or amendment.

CONSULTANT/PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT 
This Agreement made the ___ day of September, 2026 between the TOWN OF 
RIVERHEAD, a municipal corporation organized and existing under the laws of New York, 
with its office located at 4 West Second Street, Riverhead, New York 11901 (hereinafter 
referred to as the “Town”) and Theresa DeFilippis, (hereinafter referred to as 
“Consultant“). 
In consideration of the mutual promises herein contained, Town of Riverhead and 
Consultant agree as follows: 
1. SCOPE OF SERVICES 
During the term of this Agreement, Consultant shall furnish the services set forth below 
as an independent contractor and not as an employee of Town. Consultant shall provide 
services related to review of Building Department files and identification of official 
documents for electronic scanning and storage and appropriate filing and cataloging of 
such data and documents. Consultant shall not have any supervisory authority and as such 
Consultant may not independently assign work to staff, and all recommendations shall be 
referred to the Information and Technology Department Head. 
2. TERM OF AGREEMENT 
It is anticipated that Consultant shall commence work on or about September __, 2026 
and the Agreement shall terminate on or before March 31, 2027 subject to renewal with 
the approval of the CSEA or earlier termination by the Town Board if the intent of services 
rendered has been achieved.   
3. PAYMENT 
For the services identified above, Town of Riverhead will pay Consultant an hourly fee of 
FIFTY ONE DOLLARS and 00 CENTS ($51.00) not to exceed the sum of ($10,000.00)    
for all services during the term of this Agreement. The Town shall require the submission 
of time records and identification of the services provided with identification of project 
name and/or file number, together with such other standard and necessary forms required 
for payment by the Town. The Town shall not have any liability for any other expenses or 
costs incurred by the Consultant in preparation or completion of the scope of services set 
forth above.  
4. RIGHTS TO DOCUMENTS OR DATA 
Consultant acknowledges that it may have access to certain of Town’s computer and 
communication system and networks for the purposes set forth in this Agreement. If any 
data is made available or accessible to Consultant, its employees, agents or contractors, 
pertaining to the Town’s business or financial affairs or to Town’s projects, transactions, 
clients or customers or to Town officials and employees financial or personal information, 
Page 110 of 746
including information protected under HIPAA or Public Officer’s Law,  Consultant will not 
store, copy, analyze, monitor or otherwise use that data except for the purposes set forth 
in the Agreement for the benefit of Town. Consultant will comply fully with all applicable 
laws, regulations, and use and maintain physical, technical and administrative safeguards 
relating to personally identifiable information (“PII”) and data privacy with respect to any 
such data that Consultant receives or has access to under the Agreement or in connection 
with the performance of any services for Town. Consultant will otherwise protect PII and 
will not use, disclose, or transfer across borders such PII except as necessary to perform 
under the Agreement or as authorized by the data subject or in accordance with 
applicable law. To the extent that Consultant receives PII related to the performance of 
the Agreement, Consultant will protect the privacy and legal rights of Town’s personnel, 
clients, customers and contractors. Consultant agrees to hold all such information 
confidential and to not disclose the same other than to the extent required to perform its 
duties, or upon notice to and approval by the Town Supervisor, Town Attorney and 
Network Administrator, via written confirmation, that it is appropriate for Consultant to 
respond and/or pursuant to a lawful court order. The requirements of this Section shall 
survive the termination of this Agreement. 
All information and data, regardless of form, generated in the performance of, or delivered 
under this Agreement, as well as any information provided to Consultant by Town, shall 
be and remain the sole property of Town. Consultant shall keep all such information and 
data in confidence and not disclose or use it for any purpose other than in performing this 
Agreement, except with Town’s prior written approval. In the event that the legal right in 
any data and information generated in the performance of this Agreement does not vest 
in Town by law, Consultant hereby agrees and assigns to Town such legal rights in all 
such data and information. Final payment shall not be due hereunder until after receipt 
by Town of such complete document and data file, or a certification that there is no such 
information created by the services performed under this Agreement, and receipt of all 
information and data which is the property of Town. These obligations shall survive the 
termination of this Agreement. 
5. PUBLICITY 
Consultant shall not, without the prior written consent of Town, in any manner, advertise 
or publish the fact that Town has entered into this Agreement with Consultant. Consultant 
shall not, without the prior written consent of the Town, provide, release or make available 
for inspection any documents, data, written material of any kind without the prior written 
consent of at least three members of the Town board or by resolution of the Town Board, 
except to the extent that Consultant determines it necessary to retain the services of a 
third party to assist in the preparation of the audit Consultant may release the documents, 
data, and such other written material provided said third party executes a confidentiality 
agreement in favor of the Town. 
 
 
Page 111 of 746
6. ASSIGNMENT AND SUBCONTRACTING 
Performance of any part of this Agreement may not be subcontracted nor assigned 
without, in each case, the prior written consent of at least three members of the Town 
Board or by resolution of the Town Board. 
7. TERMINATION 
This Agreement may be terminated at any time by either party upon 3 days written notice 
to the other party. In the event of such termination, Town shall have no further obligation 
to Consultant, except to make any payments which may have become due under this 
Agreement. 
8. RECORDS 
Consultant shall keep accurate records of the time spent in the performance of services 
hereunder. The Town shall, until the expiration of seven years after final payment under 
this Agreement, have access to and the right to examine any directly pertinent books, 
documents, papers and records of Consultant involving transactions related to this 
Agreement. 
9. CHANGES 
The Town, by resolution of the Town Board or written request by at least three members 
of the Town Board, within the general scope of this Agreement, may, at any time by written 
notice to Consultant, issue additional instructions, require additional services or direct the 
omission of services covered by this Agreement. In such event, there will be made an 
equitable adjustment in price and time of performance, but any claim for such an 
adjustment must be made within 15 days of the receipt of such written notice. In the event 
that the Consultant determines that a change order is required, Consultant shall obtain 
written approval of the Town, by resolution or written consent of at least three members 
of the Town Board, and if the change shall require the payment of additional 
compensation, Consultant must obtain the written approval of three members of the Town 
Board or resolution of the Town Board for the additional compensation prior to 
commencement of work regarding the change order. It is agreed and understood that no 
oral agreement, conversation, or understanding between the Consultant and the Town, 
its departments, officers, agents and employees shall affect or modify any of the terms or 
obligations of this Agreement or schedules annexed hereto and made a part hereof.

Any notice shall be considered as having been given: (i) to Town of Riverhead if mailed

prepaid to Theresa DeFilippis at 449 Marcy Avenue, Riverhead, New York 11901. 
11. COMPLIANCE WITH LAWS 
Consultant shall comply with all applicable federal, state and local laws and ordinances 
and regulations in the performance of its services under this Agreement. Consultant will 
notify Town immediately if Consultant’s work for Town becomes the subject of a 
government audit or Investigation. Consultant will promptly notify Town if Consultant is

convicted of fraud of any other felony arising out of a contract with any local, state or 
federal agency. In carrying out the work required hereunder, Consultant agrees not to 
make any communication to or appearance before any person in the executive or 
legislative branches of the local, state or federal government for the purpose of influencing 
or attempting to influence any such persons in connection with the award, extension, 
continuation, renewal, amendment or modification of any contract or agreement. 
12. INSURANCE, INDEMNITY AND LIABILITY 
Consultant hereby indemnifies and holds the Town, its departments, officers, agents and 
employees, harmless against any and all claims, actions or demands against Town, its 
departments, officers, agents and employees and against any and all damages, liabilities 
or expenses, including counsel fees, arising out of the acts or omissions of Consultant 
under this Agreement, however, it is agreed and understood that the Town releases and 
holds harmless Consultant from any claims, liabilities costs, and expenses from

identified herein. 
13. CONFLICT OF INTEREST 
Consultant hereby represents and covenants that neither it nor any of its employees or 
representatives has or shall have, directly or indirectly, any agreement or arrangement 
with any official, employee or representative of the Town of Riverhead which any such 
official, employee, representative shall receive either directly or indirectly anything of 
value whether monetary or otherwise as the result of or in connection with any actual or 
contemplated application before any department of the Town, contract with the Town for 
sale of any product or service. Consultant further represents and covenants that neither 
it nor any of its employees or representatives has offered or shall offer any gratuity to the 
Town, its officers, employees, agents or representatives with a view toward obtaining this 
Agreement or securing favorable treatment with respect thereto. Consultant further 
represents that it will not engage in any activity which presents a conflict of interest in light 
of its relationship with Town.

14. DISCLOSURE 
The Town shall have the right, in its discretion, to disclose the terms and conditions of 
this Agreement (as it may be amended from time to time), including but not limited to

15. DISPUTES 
If Consultant fails to perform any of its obligations hereunder in accordance with the terms 
hereof, then after reasonable notice to Consultant not to exceed thirty (30) days, and an 
opportunity for Consultant to cure such failure (except in case of emergency), the Town 
may (but shall not be obligated to) cure such failure at the expense of the Consultant, and 
the amount incurred by the Town on demand. Notwithstanding the above, any dispute 
arising under this Agreement which is not settled by Agreement of the parties may be 
settled by appropriate legal proceedings. The Town and Consultant agree that prior to 
resorting to litigation, the matter be submitted to mediation upon the written request of 
either party and the results of such mediation shall only be binding upon agreement of 
each party to be bound thereby. The costs of mediation proceedings shall be shared 
equally by both parties. Pending any decision, appeal or judgment in such proceedings 
or the settlement of any dispute arising under this Agreement, Consultant shall proceed 
diligently with the performance of this Agreement in accordance with the decision of 
Town.

Page 117 of 746
Chapter 279. Taxation 
Article III. Veterans Exemption 
§ 279-7A. Property exempt from taxation. 
A.  1.   
 
If the ratio between the exemption granted under § 458 of the Real Property Tax Law and 
the total assessed value of the real property for which such exemption has been granted 
increased or decreased due only to the 1979 full assessment by the Town of Riverhead, 
the amount of the exemption heretofore or hereafter granted shall be increased or 
decreased in such subsequent year in the same proportion as the total assessed value 
had been increased or decreased in 1979. Such adjustment shall be made by the 
Assessors in the manner provided in § 458 of the Real Property Tax Law, and no 
application therefor need be filed by or on behalf of any owner of any eligible property. 
B. 2.   
Where property which is owned by a veteran and receiving any exemption pursuant to 
§ 458 of the Real Property Tax Law is sold and other real property is acquired to replace 
the formerly owned property, the exempt amount granted on the formerly owned property 
pursuant to this subsection and as expressed in a percentage shall be granted on the 
property acquired to replace the formerly owned property, provided that the newly 
acquired property is in the same assessing unit, and provided, further, that the exemption 
granted on the newly acquired property shall not exceed the exemption on the formerly 
owned property as expressed in a dollar amount. 
 
§ 279-7B. (1). Alternate Tax Exemption for Permanently and Totally Disabled Veterans. 
This Local Law shall be a new Section under Chapter 279  of the Town Code of the Town 
of Riverhead titled “Tax Exemption for Permanently and Totally Disabled Veterans.” 
 
§ 279-7B (2) Purpose and Findings. 
 
It is the purpose of this Local Law to exercise the authority granted to local taxing 
jurisdictions by Real Property Tax Law Section 458-a(11) which authorizes a Veterans 
Alternative Exemption. The Town Board of the Town of Riverhead finds and hereby 
determines that New York Real Property Tax Law Section 458-a(11) makes available a 
tax exemption for permanently and totally disabled veterans as a result of military service 
at the option of the local municipality. The Town Board of the Town of Riverhead further 
finds and determines that the Town of Riverhead should recognize the extraordinary 
service and sacrifice of such Veterans and the life-long hardships caused by such service 
and sacrifice.  Accordingly, the Town Board finds that exercising said option and 
Page 118 of 746
authorizing said tax exemption to furthers protections for Veterans residing within the 
Town of Riverhead. 
 
§ 279-7B(3) Grant of Property Tax Exemption for Permanently and Totally Disabled 
Veterans. 
 
Chapter 279 of the Town Code for the Town of Riverhead, “Taxation” is amended to add 
Tax Exemption for Permanently and Totally Disabled Veterans” as set forth herein. 
 
§279-7 B(4) (a) The Real Property Tax Law has been amended by the addition of a §458-
a(11), which permits the Town of Riverhead to grant a full tax exemption for the primary 
residence of any seriously disabled veteran. Said exemption is a full exemption from 
taxation and special district charges, assessments and special ad valorem levies and 
shall be hereby granted, upon application therefor and subject to the requirements set 
forth herein below: 
  
(i) Eligibility.   
 
Pursuant to §458-a(11) of the New York Real Property Tax Law, such exemption shall 
be granted provided that a veteran:  
  
A. must have been discharged or released from active military, naval, space or air 
service, including army and air national guard service pursuant to federal orders 
under title 10 of the United States code, under honorable conditions; or  
 
B. must have a qualifying condition, as defined by section one of the veterans’ 
services law, and must have received a discharge other than bad conduct or 
dishonorable from such service; or  
 
C. must be a discharged LGBT veteran, as defined in section one of the veterans’ 
services law, and must have received a discharge other than bad conduct or 
dishonorable from such service; and  
 
D. must be considered by the United States department of veterans affairs to be 
permanently and totally disabled as a result of military service, as evidenced by a 
letter, official form, or other document sent 6.2 to such veteran from such 
department that specifically states such veteran is considered to be permanently 
and totally disabled as a result of such service. 
 
(ii)    Application. 
 
Application for such exemption shall be filed with the assessor of the Town of 
Riverhead on or before the taxable status date on a form as prescribed by the 
Commissioner of Tax and Finance. 
 
Page 119 of 746
(ii) Severability.  
 
If any clause, sentence, paragraph, subdivision, section, or part of this law or the 
application thereof to any person, individual, corporation, firm, partnership, entity, or 
circumstance shall be adjudged by any court of competent jurisdiction to be invalid or 
unconstitutional, such order or judgment shall not affect, impair or invalidate the 
remainder thereof, but shall be confined in its operation to the clause, sentence, 
paragraph, subdivision, section or part of this law, or in its application to the person, 
individual, corporation, firm, partnership, entity, or circumstance directly involved in 
the controversy in which such order or judgment shall be rendered. 
 
(iii) Effective Date. 
 
This local law shall take effect upon filing with the Secretary of State pursuant to 
Section 27 of the New York Municipal Home Rule Law and the Town Code for the 
Town of Riverhead.

Recommendation of Award  
 
 
Dear Board Members: 
 
On Thursday, October 8, 2026, the Riverhead Water District (District) received bids for the installation of water 
mains along Forge Road in Riverhead.   A total of four bids were received as indicated on the attached bid tabulation. 
The lowest responsible Total Base Bid was submitted by Excav Services, Inc . of Manorville, New York. in the 
amount of $ 984,475.00.  The bid proposal also called for two Alternate Bid items that called for a substitution of 
pipe materials along the final 800 feet of the project where groundwater is anticipated during excavation.  Alternate 
Item 1A PVC substitutes PVC piping, while Alternate Item 1A HDPE substituted HDPE piping, The base bid 
specified ductile iron.  Excav Services, Inc. also submitted the lowest bid on both Alternate Items.  
 
After discussions with the Superintendent of Water, the Water District is electing to proceed with Alternate Bid Item 
1A HDPE due to its superior resistance to corrosion.  In awarding Alt. Item 1A HDPE, the quantity of pipe awarded 
under Item 1A of the bas e bid can be reduced to 50 linear feet as the piping outside the last 800 feet will remain 
ductile iron.  In addition, Item 22 can be eliminated from contract.  Based on the Alternate selection and adjustment 
to bid Items, the revised low bid amount is $947,825.00 
 
After reviewing the information submitted by the low bidder, we noted that the contractor acknowledged receipt of 
all addenda, has provided certification from New York State Dept. of Labor (NYSDOL) that they are entitled to 
perform work on public projects, and included all other documents necessary with their submission. As the sum of 
the contract exceeds $250,000,00, the low bidder has verified participation in a NYSDOL approved apprenticeship 
program. 
 
We have confirmed that Excav Services, Inc.  is a qualified and responsible contractor  and has successfully 
completed similar work for various water utilities across Long Island in the past . Including with the Town of 
Riverhead It is our opinion that Excav Services, Inc. is qualified, and their bid prices are fair and responsible . We 
recommend the Town award the contract to Excav Services, Inc. for the total bid amount of $947,825.00, as they 
are the lowest qualified bidder.

1.0 Introduction 
 
This document is the Final Scope for the Draft Generic Environmental Impact Statement (DEIS) to 
be prepared for proposed amendments to the Riverhead Town Code in order to implement the 
recommendations of the Town’s 2024 Comprehensive Plan Update as it relates to the 
development of accessory golf cottages at existing golf courses within the Town of Riverhead.  
 
The proposed action will require the mapping of a new Transfer of Development Rights (TDR) 
receiving district, and as such, a DGEIS is required to be prepared in accordance with New York 
Town Law § 261-A(2)(a), with the Town Board, as Lead Agency, having the responsibility to 
evaluate the effects of the potential action in terms of adequate resources, environmental quality 
and public facilities, including adequate transportation, water supply, waste disposal, fire 
protection, and ensuring that there will be no significant environmentally damaging 
consequences.  It is the responsibly of the Town Board to ensure that such increased 
development is compatible with the development otherwise permitted at a town, and by federal, 
state, and county agencies having jur isdiction to approve permissible development with the 
Town.  
 
The SEQRA process is intended to  provide the input and analyses necessary to ensure a “hard 
look” and assist the lead agency and other involved agencies in assessing environmental impacts 
in their decision-making process es. The document will be concise but thorough, well 
documented, accurate and consistent.  Figures and tables will be presented as applicable in 
support of the discussions and analyses contained in the document.  Technical information will 
be summarized in the body of the DGEIS and attached in their entirety in an appendix. 
 
 
 
 
Page 160 of 746
Golf Course Zoning Amendments 
DGEIS Final Scope 
 
Page 2  
2.0 Brief Description of the Proposed Action 
 
The proposed implementation of a regulatory framework to support the creation of golf cottages 
involves several actions by the Town Board, specifically including the following actions: 
 
1. Creation of a new zoning use district entitled “Golf Course (GC) Zoning Use District.” 
2. Amending the official Zoning Map of the Town of Riverhead to re-zone six (6) existing golf 
courses to the new Golf Course (GC) zoning use designation. 
3. Amending Town Code §301-3 entitled “Definitions; word usage” to include a definition of 
“Golf Cottage,” amending the definition of “Standard Golf Course.” 
4. Amending Town Code §301-208 entitled “Redemption of preservation credits” to include 
the new Golf Course (GC) zoning use district as a receiving area, identify redemption 
formula for the redemption of TDR’s as it relates to the size of golf cottages.  
5. Amending Town Code §301, Attachment 2 entitled “Residence Districts Schedule of 
Dimensional Regulations,” to include dimensional regulations for the new Golf Course 
(GC) zoning use district.  
 
In order to implement the regulatory framework to allow for the development of golf cottages,  
the following agency permits and approvals, are required: 
 
REVIEWS, PERMITS, AND APPROVALS REQUIRED

Town of Riverhead Town Board  Adoption of Local Laws

3.0 Potential Significant Impacts to be Addressed in the DGEIS 
 
The Town Board adopted a Positive Declaration on August 4, 2026 for the suite of proposed code 
amendments relating to the implementation of a regulatory framework to allow for the 
amendments to Town Code to permit the construction of golf cottages.  While the actions are 
limited in terms of scope and the affected number of parcels, and would in- and-of themselves 
not be expected to result in any significant negative environmental impacts, this DGEIS is required 
to be prepared in accordance with New York Town Law §261-A(2)(a).  The following topics along 
with applicable SEQRA DGEIS content requirements as outlined in 6 NYCRR Part 617.9 (b) of SEQR 
will be the focus of the DEIS scope and content as outlined in this Draft Scope. 
 
 
 
Page 161 of 746
Golf Course Zoning Amendments 
DGEIS Final Scope 
 
Page 3  
Impact on Groundwater 
• The DGEIS will identify the parcels targeted for potential re -zoning.  The DGEIS will include 
relevant information, including identifying each of the affected parcel’s sizes, as well as their 
locations within a Suffolk County Groundwater Management Zone (G WMZ).  A hypothetical 
analysis of a buildout of each of the affected parcels will be provided, and will include details 
regarding allowable sanitary density based on each parcel’s size and GWMZ designation.  This 
hypothetical analysis will also include a “full build-out” scenario, if every affected parcel were 
to develop golf cottages to the maximum extent possible under the proposed conditions.  
 
Impact on Transportation  
• The DGEIS will identify the parcels targeted for potential re -zoning.  The DGIES will include 
traffic data from the Town’s 2024 Comprehensive Plan Update, and will include a discussion 
of anticipated increase in traffic levels from a theoretical “full build -out” scenario of all 
affected parcels.  
 
Impacts on Aesthetic Resources 
• The DGEIS will identify the parcels targeted for re -zoning, and will include a general 
description of the character of the surrounding areas, including but not limited to the Sound 
Avenue Scenic and Historic Corridor.

major section is followed by a description of the extent and quality of information needed to 
perform the evaluation of each of the impacted resources.

10/20/2026 VII.39. 
 
 
TOWN OF RIVERHEAD 
 
TB Resolution 2026-968 
 
ACCEPTS DRAFT GENERIC ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT STATEMENT (DGEIS) FOR PROPOSED GOLF 
COUSE (GC) ZONING USE DISTRICT AMENDMENTS, SETS PUBLIC REVIEW PERIOD, SCHEDULES 
SEQRA HEARING 
 
Councilman Kern offered the following resolution,  
which was seconded by Councilwoman Merrifield 
 
          WHEREAS, by Resolution No. 2026-747, adopted on August 4, 2026, the Riverhead 
Town Board assumed Lead Agency status and issued a Positive Declaration pursuant to 
SEQRA for a series of proposed amendments to Riverhead Town Code Chapter 301, hereby 
collectively referred to as "the proposed action," in order to implement the recommendations of 
the 2024 Town of Riverhead Comprehensive Plan Update as it relates to the construction of 
accessory golf cottages on existing golf courses within the Town of Riverhead; and 
 
          WHEREAS, by Resolution No. 2026-748, the Town Board accepted a Draft Scope to be 
used for the preparation of a Draft Generic Environmental Impact Statement (DGEIS) to analyze 
the proposed action; and 
 
          WHEREAS, by Resolution adopted on October 20, 2026, the Town Board adopted a Final 
Scope to be used for the preparation of a Draft Generic Environmental Impact Statement 
(DGEIS) to analyze the proposed action; and 
 
          WHEREAS, the Planning Department has prepared the attached DGEIS, which was 
prepared based on the Final Scope, and  
 
          WHEREAS, the Town Board has reviewed the contents of the DGEIS in accordance with 
the requirements as described in 6NYCRR Part 617.9(b)(3).  Now, therefore be it 
 
           RESOLVED, that the Town Board hereby accepts the attached DGEIS, dated October 
2026, and deems the document adequate for public comment and circulation to involved 
agencies; and be it further 
 
           RESOLVED, that the Planning Department is hereby authorized to file the DGEIS with 
the Town Clerk, circulate the DGEIS to involved and interested agencies, post a digital version 
of the DGEIS on the Town of Riverhead's website; and be it further 
 
           RESOLVED, that the Town Board desires to hold a public hearing on the DGEIS; and be 
it further 
 
           RESOLVED, that the Town Clerk is hereby authorized to publish the attached public 
notice to schedule the required SEQRA Public Hearing once in the October 29th, 2026 issue of 
the of the News Review newspaper hereby designated as the official newspaper for this 
purpose 
 
           RESOLVED, that the Town Clerk is hereby authorized to forward a copy of this resolution 
Page 171 of 746
to the Planning Department, the Office of the Town Attorney; and be it further, 
 
          RESOLVED, that all Town Hall Departments may review and obtain a copy of this 
resolution from the electronic storage device and if needed, a certified copy of same may be 
obtained from the Office of the Town Clerk. 
 
 
 
 
THE VOTE 
 
RESULT: 
 
MOVER: Councilman Robert Kern 
SECONDER: Councilwoman Denise Merrifield 
AYES: None 
NAYS: None

1.0 Executive Summary 
This document is the Draft Generic Environmental Impact Statement (DGEIS) , which will study 
the potential environmental impacts of the implementation of a series of amendments to the 
Riverhead Town Code which will form the regulatory framework necessary to implement the 
recommendations of the Town of Riverhead 2024 Comprehensiv e Plan Update (2024 CPU), 
adopted in September 2024, as it relates to the creation of golf cottages on existing golf courses 
within the Town of Riverhead.  
Because the amendments to Town Code will require the creation and mapping of new Transfer 
of Development Rights (TDR) receiving districts, the Town Board, as Lead Agency, is required to 
prepare a Generic Environmental Impact Statement, pursuant to New York  Town Law §261 -
A(2)(a). 
The Town Board, by Resolution No. 2026-747, adopted on August 4, 2026, assumed Lead Agency 
Status, and issued a Positive Declaration pursuant to SEQRA, requiring the preparation of a DGEIS.  
By Resolution No. 2026-748, also adopted on August 4, 2026, the T own Board accepted a Draft 
Scope to be used for the preparation of a DGEIS, and set a twenty -one (21) day public review 
comment period, with the record being left open until the end of day on August 25, 2026 for the 
submission of written comments on the Draft Scope. 
2.0 Description of the Proposed Action 
The proposed implementation of the regulatory framework to support the creation of golf 
cottages involves several actions by the Town Board relating to the Town’s Zoning Ordinance 
(Chapter 301 of the Riverhead Town Code).  The following amendments are collectively referred 
to as “the proposed action” for the purposes of SEQRA analysis: 
1. Creation of a new zoning use district entitled “Golf Course (GC) Zoning Use District” 
2. Amending the official Zoning Map of the Town of Riverhead to re-zone six (6) existing 
golf courses to the new Golf Course (GC) zoning use designation. 
3. Amending Town Code §301 -3 entitled “Definitions; word usage” to include a 
definition of “Golf Cottage,” as well as amending the definition of “Standard Golf 
Course.”  
4. Amending Town Code §301 -208 entitled “Redemption of Preservation Credits” to 
include the new Golf Course (GC) zoning use district as a receiving area, as well as 
identify the redemption formula for the redemption of TDR’s as it relates to golf 
cottages. 
5. Amending Town Code §301, Attachment 2 entitled “Residence Districts Schedule of 
Dimensional Regulations,” to include dimensional regulations for the new Golf Course 
(GC) zoning use district.  
The creation of the new GC zoning use district, and its application to six (6) existing golf courses 
located within the Town of Riverhead, specifically The Rock Golf Club in Wading River, the Baiting 
Page 177 of 746
Golf Course Zoning Use District – Draft Generic Environmental Impact Statement  
 
5 | Page  
 
Hollow Club in Baiting Hollow, Friars Head, Cherry Creek Golf Links, the Woods at Cherry Creek, 
and the Long Island National Golf Club in Riverhead, as well as the amendments to the Town 
Code’s definition of a “standard golf course” would make the existing  golf courses conforming 
within the new GC zoning use district, and would eliminate the need for a special permit for the 
construction of golf cottages, which would currently constitute the expansion of a pre -existing 
non-conforming use within the existing  Residence A-80 or Agricultural Protection (APZ) zoning 
use districts in which the golf courses are currently located.  The amendments would also 
establish a definition of a golf cottage, and set TDR redemption rates for golf cottage uses, which 
are currently proposed at a rate of 1,200 square foot of floor area per TDR credit redeemed.  The 
proposed action would also create a GC zoning use designation in the Town’s Residence Schedule 
of Dimensional Regulations, which exactly mirrors the existing RA80 and APZ dimensional 
regulations (i.e. a minimum lot size of 80,000 square feet, or two “builder’s acres” per residential 
lot), thereby establishing consistency with the existing zoning without creating the potential for 
increased residential development in the event a golf course closes and the owner elects to 
redevelop a site with a residential subdivision.  Certain other protections are built into the 
proposed GC zoning use district, including the requirement for cluster development in the event 
a golf course is redeveloped into a residential subdivision, which is also a requirement in the 
existing RA-80 and APZ zoning use districts.  
The metrics below are provided in order to clearly identify a theoretical maximum buildout, TDR 
redemption, and monetary value of the land preservation: 
• 6 golf courses x 1 unit per hole x 18 holes per course = 108 units 
 
• 108 units x 600 sq. ft. per unit = 64,800 sq. ft. of building development 
 
• 64,800 sq. ft. ÷ 1200 sq. ft. per TDR = 54 TDR’s for full buildout 
 
• 54 TDR’s x 43,560 sq. ft. of land preserved per TDR = 2,352,240 sq. ft. of land 
preservation 
 
• $80,000 value per TDR x 54 TDR’s = $4,320,000 preservation cost 
2.1 Introduction 
2.2 Project Background, Needs, and Objectives 
2.2.1 Project Background 
Chapter 14 of the Town of Riverhead’s 2024 Comprehensive Plan Update included a 
recommendation to consider allowing for golf cottages as an accessory use on golf courses (in 
any zoning district) with the use of TDR credits (Page 207, 2024 CPU).  The plan stated this would 
be an accessory use on or adjacent to a golf course, with golf cottages being intended to provide 
Page 178 of 746
Golf Course Zoning Use District – Draft Generic Environmental Impact Statement  
 
6 | Page  
 
convenient lodging for golfers or visitors who want to stay close to the golf course for a short 
stay.  The plan noted that golf cottages are not meant to be used for long -term housing, which 
was considered in the drafting of the proposed definition of a g olf cottage, where the proposed 
definition includes language which states that “Golf cottages shall not be used for the purposes 
of establishing residency within the Town of Riverhead.”   
The 2024 CPU also included a proposed redemption formula for the use of TDR’s as it relates to 
golf cottages, and recommended a rate of 1 TDR per golf cottage, and capped the size of a golf 
cottage at a maximum of 600 square feet per unit.  At the current trading rate for TDR’s 
(approximately $80,000 per TDR credit, based on a recent contract of sale for an existing TDR 
Certificate, Certificate No. 15.01), the initial cost of TDR’s for a golf course to construct eighteen 
cottages, which is the maximum allow able build out for a standard golf course, would be 
approximately $1,440,000.  This cost does not include permitting, engineering, and construction, 
and represents only the cost for the right to construct the cottages.   
After the Planning Department’s initial drafting of amendments to the Town Code, the 
amendments were presented to and discussed with the Town Board at its work session on 
September 17, 2025.  At that work session, a majority of Town Board felt that the up -front TDR 
cost, which was presented the at the recommended rate of one (1) TDR per cottage, could 
potentially be a financial deterrent for a golf course owner seeking to create golf cottages.  The 
Town Board subsequently requested a change the redemption f ormula for golf cottages from 
one (1) TDR per cottage to a redemption rate of 1,200 square feet of floor area for golf cottage 
use per preservation credit, effectively cutting the TDR redemption rate recommended by the 
2024 CPU in half. It is acknowledged, however, that the 2024 CPU does recommend revisiting the 
transfer formula periodically in order to ensure that redemption rates are appropriately 
calibrated to both maximize the use of TDR credits without overburdening potential projects. 
The code was amended, at the Town Board’s direction, and discussed again at its work session 
on December 11, 2025.  A public hearing on the code amendments was subsequently scheduled 
by the Town Board, and held on January 21, 2026.  At that meeting, public comment was received 
and considered, which resulted in the re-working of the proposed code amendment to its current 
form being considered in this DGEIS. 
2.2.2 Public Needs and Town Objectives 
The 2024 CPU, specifically Chapter 4: Economic Development, speaks extensively about 
enhancing and expanding tourism opportunities, as the tourism industry has become a steady 
economic driver for Riverhead since the 1990’s as the North Fork emerged as a prominent tourist 
destination with attractions such as Long Island wind country, historic downtown, Splish Splash 
water park, the Long Island Aquarium, Tanger Mall, the Suffolk Theater, as well as numerous 
farm-stands and agritourism destinations.  The Town’ s goals in the implementation of the 
creation of golf cottage zoning are twofold, first is to increase tourism opportunities, as visitors 
to the North Fork who take advantage of a golf cottage stay are likely to spend money at the 
Page 179 of 746
Golf Course Zoning Use District – Draft Generic Environmental Impact Statement  
 
7 | Page  
 
Town’s tourist destinations.  Second is the increased usage of the Town’s TDR program.  If the six 
(6) proposed golf courses targeted for the proposed re -zoning were to all develop golf cottages 
at the maximum allowable densities under the proposed framewo rk, which would be eighteen 
(18) cottages each at 600 square feet (totaling 64,800 square feet), at a TDR redemption rate of 
1,200 square feet per TDR, the result would be 54 acres.  Based on the current trading rate of 
approximately $80,000.00 per TDR (as  noted above, based on a recent TDR transaction), the 
resulting benefit of 54 TDR would equate to approximately $4,320,000.00 of private funds to 
preserve the 54 acres.  
2.2.3 Benefits of the Proposed Action 
As drafted, the proposed series of code amendments would create a framework and regulatory 
structure to accomplish one of the recommendations of the 2024 CPU, while simultaneously 
bolstering the Town’s TDR program.  Protections written into the current dra ft will allow for 
preservation of the Sound Avenue Scenic and Historic Corridor, by establishing a minimum 300 -
foot setback from Sound Avenue, as well as protect other neighboring properties by establishing 
a minimum 125-foot setback from all other property lines.  
In creating the regulatory framework to allow for the creation of golf cottages, the Town Board 
has elected to consider a series of amendments to the Town Code that will accomplish the 
following goals: 
1. Allow for golf courses within the Town to construct golf cottages to help foster 
tourism opportunities within the Town, and further support the economic success of 
the golf industry within the Town.  
2. Serve as a potential vehicle for land preservation through the use of TDR’s. 
3. Increase the Town’s tax base by adding value to existing golf courses.

3.0 Natural Environmental Resources 
3.1 Water Resources 
3.1.1 Existing Conditions 
The proposed action has the potential to increase demand for public water as well as increase 
sanitary density loading related to future development.  In order to understand existing 
conditions, the DGEIS will detail the existing conditions for water resources, including identifying 
existing golf course locations within Riverhead Water District extensions, describe existing 
infrastructure, as well as describe existing golf course locations within Suffolk County 
Groundwater Management Zones (SCGWMZ), and detail requirements of Suffolk County Sanitary 
Code Article 6.  
The six existing golf courses, described in Section 2.0 of this DGEIS, are located within the 
following Riverhead Water District Extensions: 
1. The Rock Golf Club: Located within Riverhead Water District Extension No. 35. 
2. Baiting Hollow Club: Located partially within both Riverhead Water District Extension 
No. 20 (Sound Avenue), and Extension No. 26 (Fresh Pond Landing & Vicinity). 
3. Friar’s Head: Located partially within both Riverhead Water District Extension No. 23 
(Reeve’s, Rollingwood, & Dolphin), and Extension No. 31. 
4. Cherry Creek Golf Links : Located within Riverhead Water District Extension No. 19c 
(Woodfield Meadows). 
5. The Woods at Cherry Creek : Located within Riverhead Water District Extension No. 
65 (Woods at Cherry Creek). 
6. Long Island National Golf Club: Located within Riverhead Water District Extension No. 
95 (Northville). 
All of the above referenced golf courses are currently served by the Riverhead Water District’s 
existing infrastructure, which include 12-inch water mains located within public roadways which 
front all of the proposed sites, including along Sound Avenue, N orthville Turnpike, Reeves 
Avenue, as well as Fairway Drive. 
Suffolk County is broken up into eight (8) distinct GWMZ’s, all of which have an allowable sanitary 
density of 600 gallons per day (gpd) per acre, with the exception of GWMZ Nos. III, V, or VI, where 
the allowable density is 300 gpd per acre.  The Town of Riverhead is generally located within

9 | Page  
 
either GWMZ III, IV, or VIII, as described below.  The allowable sanitary density of a specific 
property is determined by multiplying the adjusted gross lot area in acres (43,560 square feet per 
acre), by the allowable gpd based on the underlying GWMZ.  The location of the six existing golf 
courses, described in Section 2.0 of this DGEIS, existing SCGWMZ’s, as well as the size of the 
respective parcels are and their allowable sanitary densities pursuant to Suffolk County Sanitary 
Code Article 6, are identified as follows: 
1. The Rock Golf Club: Located within SCGWMZ Zone VIII, with an allowable sanitary 
density of 600 gallons per day (gpd) per acre.  The property size is approximately 132 
acres, with an allowable sanitary density of approximately 79,200 gpd. 
2. Baiting Hollow Club : Located within SCGWMZ Zone VIII, with an allowable sanitary 
density of 600 gpd per acre.  The property size is approximately 155 acres, with an

with an allowable sanitary density of approximately 90,000  gpd. 
3.1.2 Anticipated Impacts 
The Suffolk County Department of Health Services (SCDHS) Office Division of Environmental 
Quality’s July 21, 2020 “Standards for Approval of Plans and Construction for Sewage Disposal 
Systems for Other Than Single -Family Residences” (Reference 1.1) contain s guidance for 
determining sanitary density rates for uses other than single -family residences.  Based on the 
nature of a golf cottage, in that it is not to be used as a residence, but operates more akin to a 
transient lodging unit, such as a hotel, it is presumed that each golf cottage would be treated by 
the Department of Health Services as a “motel/hotel unit.” The SCDHS guidance document 
prescribes a sanitary flow of 150 gpd for a motel/hotel unit exceeding 400 square feet.  In the 
event that a golf course seeks to develop the maximum number of cottages allowable under the 
proposed action, or eighteen cottages, the presumed sanitary density rate would be 2,700 gpd, 
which is well below the allowable sanitary densities permitted on each of the six golf courses 
targeted for the proposed re-zoning.   
The Riverhead Water District utilizes the above referenced SCHDS standards in determining 
anticipated potable water demand, plus additional flow for fire suppression, which is determined 
Page 182 of 746
Golf Course Zoning Use District – Draft Generic Environmental Impact Statement  
 
10 | Page  
 
based on site specific factors such as size and type of building, use and occupancy, as well as 
location.  
It is acknowledged that the golf courses targeted for the proposed re -zoning have existing 
sanitary density loads from clubhouses which often include restaurants and bars, maintenance 
buildings, other improvements, and potentially from the maintenance of the golf course grounds 
themselves.  Ultimately, as the SCDHS maintains jurisdiction over the final use, lot area, design 
and location of the sewage disposal and water supply systems, review and approval from the 
SCDHS will be required before any constructi on can begin.  Any site plan application submitted 
to the Town for the construction of golf cottages would be referred to the SCDHS for review and 
comment prior to any approval action by the Planning Board.  
It is also noted that the creation and implementation of the GC zoning use district does not create 
any change in the permissible number of single-family residences that would be permitted under 
the current zoning, as the underlying base density remains at one single-family residence per two 
“builder’s acre” (80,000 square foot minimum lot size).  As such, there are no anticipated impacts 
related to residential development resulting from the change of zone from either APZ or RA -80 
to the new GC zoning use designation.  
3.1.3 Proposed Mitigation 
The proposed action is not anticipated to require any mitigation, as all of the golf course parcels 
targeted for re -zoning are located within existing Riverhead Water District extensions and are 
already served by public water, and the potential increase in  sanitary density from the 
construction of golf cottages falls within the permissible sanitary densities established by the 
SCHDS.  Never-the-less, any site plan application submitted to the Town will be referred to both 
the Riverhead Water District and SC DHS for review and approvals based on site specific 
proposals.  Approval from the SCDHS will be required prior to the issuance of any building 
permits.

3.2.2 Anticipated Impacts 
The current draft of the proposed amendments to the Riverhead Town Code includes significant 
setbacks for golf cottages, including a minimum 125-foot setback from any property line, as well 
as a significantly increased setback of a minimum of 300 feet from  Sound Avenue.  These 
proposed setbacks exceed the existing minimum setback requirements for the RA80 and APZ 
zoning use districts, which currently require a 60 -foot front yard setback, a 30 -foot/65 foot 
combined side yard setback, and a 75 -foot rear yard setback.  Additional protections built into 
the proposed code amendments include the requirement that golf cottages shall be sited in such 
a manner that minimized visibility of structures from public roadways and neighboring 
properties.   
Regarding the rezoning of the targeted parcels from either RA80 or APZ to the proposed GC 
zoning use district, all dimensional regulations for the GC zoning use district are exactly consistent 
with those required in the RA80 and APZ, so there are no anticipated impacts from potential 
redevelopment of any of these courses into residential subdivisions that would be a deviation 
from that which is already permitted under the existing zoning. 
3.2.3 Proposed Mitigation 
With due consideration given to the enhanced setbacks for golf cottages from existing property 
lines, as well as the significantly enhanced setback from the Historic Sound Avenue corridor, no 
additional mitigation measures are proposed.  It is noted that a ny application for golf cottages 
that is submitted to the Town for site plan approval must include architectural elevations, which 
will be reviewed by the Town’s Architectural Review Board, as well as the Planning Board, to 
ensure compatibility with existing community character.

4.1.2 Anticipated Impacts 
Similar to section 3.1.2, where demand and sanitary densities would be expected to be similar to 
a hotel/motel use, the proposed golf cottages would operate in a similar manner and would be 
expected to have a similar trip generation and traffic impacts to a hotel/motel. 
The Institute of Transportation Engineers Trip Generation Manual, 12 th Edition, Volume 3 
(Reference 1.5), Land Use Code 320 (Motel), indicates an average vehicle trip generation 
between 0.33 trips per AM peak hour, and 0.3 vehicle trips per PM peak hour, with the range of 
rates falls between 0.12 and 0.62 vehicle trips per room.   
For the purposes of this DGEIS, and in order to establish a thoroughly conservative estimate of 
the vehicle trip generation at a given location, the highest value of the range of trip generation 
(0.62 trips per room) will be utilized. 
In the scenario where a golf course that avails themselves of the ability to construct up to 
eighteen (18) cottages on their course, the anticipated increase in vehicle trips would be 
approximately 11.16 vehicle trips per hour (0.62 trips per room multiplied by 18 rooms per 
course).   
The New York State Department of Environmental Conservation’s Full Environmental Assessment 
Form Workbook (Reference 1.2) provides guidance for reviewing agencies to assist in 
understanding location, size, and characteristics of a proposed project.  Per the NYSDEC’s 
guidance, a project would be considered to have a “significant increase” in traffic if the project is 
expected to produce in excess of 100 vehicle trips per peak hour per day (FEAF Workbook, Page 
52).  The conservative estimate of 11 vehicle trips per hour falls well below the NYSDEC’s 
threshold of significant traffic impacts.  
4.1.3 Proposed Mitigation 
As the existing golf courses are located on existing Town or County roadways, and based on the 
minimal anticipated increased vehicular trip generation, no traffic mitigation is proposed in 
connection with the anticipated increased development.  
5.0 Other Required Sections  
5.1 Cumulative Impacts 
In order to take a “hard look” at the potential cumulative impacts of the proposed re-zoning, this 
section will assume a full-buildout of the six-existing golf courses targeted for the proposed Golf 
Course re-zoning. 
Page 187 of 746
Golf Course Zoning Use District – Draft Generic Environmental Impact Statement  
 
15 | Page  
 
As discussed in Section 3.1.2 above, the anticipated increase in water demand for a golf course 
seeking to construct eighteen cottages is 2,700 gpd of domestic, plus potential additional 
demand for fire suppression.  In the event that all six golf courses developed golf cottages to the 
maximum extent allowed under the proposed code amendments, the total anticipated increase 
in domestic water usage would be approximately 16,200 gpd.  The Riverhead Water District, 
based on its 2025 Pumpage Data Report ( Reference 1.3), which was provided to the NYSDEC, 
experienced a peak daily pumping rate of 17,935,000 gallons.  The potential increase generated 
by a full build out of golf cottages would equate to an approximately 0.009% increase in the peak 
daily pumping rate.  
As also discussed in Section 3.1.2 above, the anticipated increase in sanitary density for a golf 
course seeking to construct eighteen cottages is 2,700 gpd per course.  Full buildout of the six 
courses targeted for the proposed re -zoning would equate to a n increased sanitary density of 
16,200 gpd, where the total allowable sanitary density by SCDHS standards is 648,000 gpd, based 
on the total acreage of the golf courses.  This increase constitutes 2.5% of the total allowable 
sanitary density of the existing golf courses.  
As discussed in Section 4.1.2, the anticipated increase in vehicle trip generation based on a golf 
course seeking to build eighteen cottages is approximately 11 vehicle trips per peak hour.  A full 
buildout of the six courses targeted for re -zoning would be expected to result in approximately 
66 additional vehicle trips per peak hour.  Based on the geographic dispersion of the parcels 
targeted for rezoning, as well as existing AADT’s and LOS’s throughout the Town, a full buildout 
of golf cottages is not expected to result in any significant impacts.  
6.0 Alternatives  
6.1 Alternative 1: No Action Alternative 
The no -action alternative would result in no change from the existing zoning and land use 
patterns at the sites targeted for rezoning.  While the no -action alternative would not result in 
any increased demand for water usage, increase in sanitary density, or increase in vehicular trip 
generation, there would also be no increase in land preservation through the use of TDR’s, nor 
would there be an opportunity for the Town to foster and grow the tourism sector of the Town’s 
economy. 
In the no action alternative, in the event a golf course closes and abandons operation in favor of 
the development of a residential subdivision, each site, with the exception of Great Rock and the 
Baiting Hollow Club due to existing restrictions placed on those properties connected to prior 
development approvals, could be developed under the existing two-acre zoning regulations.  The 
total acreage of the four remaining golf courses (Cherry Creek, The Woods at Cherry Creek, Long 
Island National, and Friar’s Head) is approximately 793 acres, which would yield approximately 
397 new single-family residences, based on the minimum required lot size of 80,000 sq. ft.

Golf Course Zoning Use District – Draft Generic Environmental Impact Statement

Anticipated water demand from 397 new single -family residences would be approximately 
119,100 gallons per day, plus irrigation, based on SCDHS standards for single-family residenc 
6.2 Alternative 2: Re-Zoning of Existing Golf Courses to Residence A-80 (RA80) Zoning Use 
District*.  
The Residence A -80 (RA80) zoning use district is already a TDR receiving district, pursuant to 
Riverhead Town Code §301 -205A, which would allow the use of TDR’s in the district.  If the 
existing golf courses were targeted for a potential rezoning to RA80, it would require and 
amendment to the Zoning Use district to allow for the creation of golf cottages with TDR’s, and 
would also require an amendment to Town Code §301 -208 to set the TDR redemption value as 
it relates to golf cottages. 
In addition to allowing for the potential development of golf cottages under the RA80 zoning use 
district, rezoning golf courses to RA80 has the potential to increase the allowable residential 
density.  Pursuant to Town Code §301 -208A, the use of TDR’s per mits a developer to increase 
the development yield of a tract of RA80 land to one lot per 40,000 square feet, or double the 
density which would currently be permitted under the proposed Golf Course zoning use district 
designation.  Under the proposed Golf Course zoning designations, Friar’s Head (349 acres), Long 
Island National (150 acres), Cherry Creek (166 acres) and the Woods at Cherry Creek (128 acres), 
which total approximately 793 acres, in the event of residential redevelopment, could yield ±397 
new single-family residences based on the proposed development density of one lot per 80,000 
sq. ft.  
In the alternative scenario where the courses were re -zoned to RA80, the ±397 single -family 
residences that could be developed on the courses would double to ±794 single -family 
residences.  In this scenario, it is acknowledged that there would be a signifi cant use of TDR’s, 
approximately 397, in order to achieve the maximum allowable density under the RA80 zoning 
designation.  
The potential increase in residential density afforded under the RA80 zoning designation would 
have the potential to increase water demand by a minimum of 119,100 gpd (based on the 
SCDHS’s sanitary flow of 300 gpd per single-family residence, multiplied by the 397-unit increase), 
plus water for irrigation, as opposed to the 16,200 gpd of additional water usage from a full 
buildout of golf cottages across all six courses identified for rezoning.   
Similarly, sanitary density would increase by 119,100 gpd, again, based on the SCDHS standards 
for a single-family residence. 
Although the threshold for significant traffic impacts resulting from single -family residential 
subdivisions are relatively high, with the NYSDEC’s FEAF workbook identifying the threshold for 
significant impacts at 95 units, each of the courses under a potential RA80 rezoning, could be 
redeveloped with new single -family residences which exceed this threshold, resulting in

additional mitigation measures, such as the installation of traffic signals, road widening, re -
striping, etc.
